Hi Maria,

Attached two quick artifacts: pulse-weekly-usage-20270903-09.pdf (7-day telemetry) and roi-summary-pulseai-202709.xlsx. Quick summary of what we see:

- Token spend: Sep MTD ~ 1.1M tokens (35% increase vs. Aug); run-rate suggests Oct could hit ~1.5M without intervention.
- Embeddings: 40% of token spend but 55% of inference time due to batch patterns.
- Latency: p50 ~ 110ms, p95 ~ 420ms (spike correlated with longer generation prompts).
- Unit economics: blended cost per 1k tokens (hosted) ~ $0.21 after current credits; effective ROI on RAG queries still strong but margin tight for high-throughput endpoints.

Given the trajectory, you may see overages against the current commit in mid-Oct. Two short paths we usually recommend: (1) add a stepped commit (e.g., 750k monthly with a 10% discount for the delta) or (2) short dedicated pool for high-throughput endpoints (reduces per-token cost ~20% but requires a 30-day provisioning window).

Can we book 30 minutes next week to walk these options with Marcus (cc'd) and get an indication of procurement timing? If you prefer, Marcus can pull together a line-item amendment for legal.

Thanks,

Hi Maria — looping in Laura for renewal/contract details. Priya, thanks for the summary. I put together three practical options (attached as proposed-commit-options-REDWOOD.pdf and a quick cost workbook redwood-dedicated-estimate-750k.xlsx):

Option A — Short-term buffer (fast, no amendment):
- Add one-time burst credit of 300k tokens (applied to Oct)
- No change to commit; no billing delay
- Good if the forecast bump is temporary

Option B — Stepped commit + discount (recommended if growth persists):
- Commit: 750k tokens/month for 6 months
- Delta priced at 10% off list for tokens above current commit up to new commit
- Overage beyond 750k billed at standard overage rate (we can tier this in contract)
- Estimated effective blended unit cost reduction of ~12% vs current run-rate

Option C — Dedicated pool pilot (best $/token for steady volume):
- Dedicated capacity sized for peak (provisioned in 30–45 days)
- 12-week pilot with 20% lower per-token execution cost; 30% sustained discount if convert to annual reserved capacity
- Requires a short SLA addendum and 60-day notice for termination

Notes: the p95 latency spikes are most easily addressed by routing heavier prompts to the dedicated pool or by using short-circuit caching for repetitive embeddings. I've annotated the attached workbook with expected cost lines for each option and the impact on Oct billing if committed by Oct 6.

If you want, we can do a 30-min call Thursday or Friday next week to walk the workbook together and I can produce a line-item amendment for legal after we agree on Option B or C.

Thanks,
